Make FixedAgent handle being unplaced as agreed in #3748

### Pre-PR Checklist
- [x] This PR is a bug fix, not a new feature or enhancement.

### Summary
A `FixedAgent` that hasn't been placed in a cell yet crashed with an unclear `AttributeError` in two places. This makes it follow the rules agreed with @quaquel in #3748: assigning `None` before placement is fine, and removing an unplaced agent is an error, raised clearly and before anything is changed.

### Bug / Issue
Fixes #3748. The behaviour below is from the discussion there ([1](https://github.com/mesa/mesa/issues/3748#issuecomment-6401281779), [2](https://github.com/mesa/mesa/issues/3748#issuecomment-6401594696)).

A fixed agent gets its cell once, after it's created, so it starts out unplaced:

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    direction LR
    [*] --> Unplaced: FixedAgent(model)
    Unplaced --> Unplaced: cell = None (no-op)
    Unplaced --> Placed: cell = some_cell
    Placed --> Removed: remove()
    Unplaced --> Unplaced: remove() raises ValueError, agent untouched
    Placed --> Placed: cell = None or another cell raises ValueError
```

What changes:

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| unplaced, `agent.cell = None` | `AttributeError` | no-op, stays unplaced |
| unplaced, `remove()` | deregisters from the model, then `AttributeError` | `ValueError` with a clear message, agent untouched |
| placed, `cell = None` or another cell | `ValueError` | unchanged |
| placed, `remove()` | works | unchanged |

The second row was the worst one: the agent was already gone from `model.agents` by the time the error came up, so it ended up half removed.

### Implementation
Two guard clauses in `mesa/discrete_space/cell_agent.py`, so the normal path is unchanged:

- `FixedCell.cell` setter: return early when assigning `None` to an unplaced agent.
- `FixedAgent.remove()`: check for a cell first and raise `ValueError` before calling `super().remove()`.

The new error reads:

```
ValueError: Cannot remove FixedAgent 1: it is not in a cell. A fixed agent has to be placed in a cell before it can be removed.
```

I went with `ValueError` to match the existing "Cannot move agent in FixedCell" error. Happy to switch both to a `SpaceException` if you'd prefer that.

As agreed, `model.remove_all_agents()` still raises when the model has an unplaced fixed agent, now with this message instead of the `AttributeError`.

### Testing
Four tests in `tests/discrete_space/test_discrete_space.py`:
- assigning `None` while unplaced is a no-op, and the agent can still be placed afterwards
- `remove()` on an unplaced agent raises and the agent is still in `model.agents`
- a second `remove()` after a successful one raises
- assigning `None` after placement still raises (unchanged behaviour, kept as a guard)

The first three fail on `main` and pass here. The full suite passes with `pytest tests/ -W error` (937 passed), and `pre-commit` is clean. I also ran the `mesa-examples` suite against this branch: 5 example files use `FixedAgent` and all 25 tests pass, so nothing there relies on removing an unplaced fixed agent.

fix(agentset): downgrade _HardKeyAgentSet.select_random() to AgentSet (#3992)

## Description

### Background & Problem
In `_HardKeyAgentSet` (which backs `model.agents` and `model.agents_by_type[...]`), the internal dictionary stores strong references to keep active agents alive. However, to prevent memory leaks when agents are removed from the model, **all user-facing views returned by `_HardKeyAgentSet` must be downgraded to standard `AgentSet` (weak references via `WeakKeyDictionary`) when `inplace=False`**:

https://github.com/mesa/mesa/blob/b1db02ad/mesa/agentset.py#L923-L942

While methods like `select()`, `copy()`, `shuffle()`, `sort()`, and `groupby()` all correctly implement this downgrade, `select_random()` was missing an override in `_HardKeyAgentSet`. 

Consequently, calling `model.agents.select_random(...)` inherited `AbstractAgentSet.select_random()`, which defaults to returning `type(self)(...)` (a `_HardKeyAgentSet`). This retained strong references to the sampled agents. When those agents were removed via `agent.remove()`, Python's garbage collector was prevented from freeing them, causing an unbounded memory leak in simulations that sample agents across steps.

### Solution
This PR adds the `select_random()` override to `_HardKeyAgentSet`, bringing it into full parity with `select()`, `shuffle()`, and `sort()`:
- **`inplace=False` (default):** Downgrades the returned sample to standard `AgentSet` (weak references), allowing removed agents to be garbage collected properly.
- **`inplace=True`:** Updates and returns `self` (`_HardKeyAgentSet`), preserving expected in-place mutation behavior.

### Testing
- Added `test_hardkeyagentset_select_random_garbage_collection()` in `tests/test_agentset.py` verifying with `weakref.ref` and `gc.collect()` that dead agents are successfully freed after removal.
- Extended `test_hardkeyagentset_downgrade()` to verify that `hard_set.select_random()` returns `AgentSet` (not `_HardKeyAgentSet`) when `inplace=False`, and returns `_HardKeyAgentSet` when `inplace=True`.
- 100% diff coverage verified; all 52 `AgentSet` tests pass.

Fixes #3992
